findings.text: Reviewer confirmed non-tautology with four independent one-line source mutations (proceed past a red gate, proceed past a fail verdict, skip review human_minutes, force the loop_respected invariant true); each was caught by the selftest and restored, and the baseline returns to 728 passed / 0 failed.

When a human step returns decision rejected with no note, the run still ends in state ready with the merge-readiness go-ahead text rather than a rejection-specific message; this matches the documented design (the executor records the human decision, it does not author it) and is non-blocking.

summary: X1 (WARP-0401, Executor v1) is correct and honest. Independent adversarial review: pass_with_notes, 0 blocking, gate GREEN (selftest 728). The reviewer drove the Executor over its own fake seam - the happy path reaches merge_ready and records human_minutes equal to the emitted-events sum, a red gate and a fail verdict each HALT before evidence and merge, two failed review cycles re-drive the build twice then stop for a human, and non-ready, plan-refusal, build-fail, and bad-proof each halt at their step - and proved non-tautology with four one-line source mutations (proceed-past-red-gate, proceed-past-fail-verdict, skip-human_minutes, force-invariant-true), each caught by the selftest and restored. Capabilities executor_driver=mechanical (control logic gate-tested over a fake seam) + executor_agent_dispatch=procedure (build/review/approve delegated, LiveLoop fails loud) are both honest per the manifest vocabulary; both capabilities.yaml copies byte-identical; stdlib only; proportionate (a driver over existing seams, no daemon or service); generic; ASCII. proof_digest recomputed via validate.py.
